builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Context Is Not Free: Carbon-Aware LLM Routing for Multi-Turn LLM Web Services across Geo-Distributed Data Centers
summary: CarbonRouter replaces carbon-aware routers that treat each query independently by jointly selecting model, GPU type, and region per turn while charging KV-cache history recomputation to any candidate deployment that lacks the session's cache, plus a gate that avoids oscillating a session between regions. The cost is a cache-aware carbon cost model fed by cached-token counts from serving backends and online routing logic per turn, which adds control-plane complexity on top of the serving stack. It can fail when cached-token telemetry is unavailable or inaccurate, when carbon-intensity forecasts for grid regions are stale, or when the oscillation gate pins sessions to a region whose carbon intensity later worsens.
rationale: The method presupposes geo-distributed deployments across multiple regions, GPU types, and models, which the reader's single-GPU or API-based infrastructure does not have, so it is worth tracking but not adoptable in their production practice.

claims.statement: CarbonRouter replaces carbon-aware routers that treat each query independently by jointly selecting model, GPU type, and region per turn while charging KV-cache history recomputation to any candidate deployment that lacks the session's cache, plus a gate that avoids oscillating a session between regions. The cost is a cache-aware carbon cost model fed by cached-token counts from serving backends and online routing logic per turn, which adds control-plane complexity on top of the serving stack. It can fail when cached-token telemetry is unavailable or inaccurate, when carbon-intensity forecasts for grid regions are stale, or when the oscillation gate pins sessions to a region whose carbon intensity later worsens.

Reduces CO2 emissions by 16.1% on average relative to FairCarbon, a state-of-the-art carbon-aware router, rising to 23.1% for sessions longer than 30 turns, while also improving predicted answer quality and estimated latency.
